newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks weaker, hit by Thai baht concerns.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks weaker, hit by Thai baht concerns.

text.p: Singapore shares were weaker on Thursday as institutional investors began a sell down in response to the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS) intervention to prop up the struggling Thai baht, a dealer said.
"It has triggered selling from the programme buyers who are now cutting their exposures," a dealer with a local firm said.
The MAS took joint action with the Bank of Thailand on Wednesday to stem speculation in the baht.
At the 0430 GMT lunchtime break, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 30.29 at 2,067.97, with 1.4 percent shed from the value of the index.
"Some of the funds are getting a bit uneasy about our involvement with the baht," the dealer said.
Key losers in the morning session were bank stocks, the main victims of tensions several weeks ago about their Thai exposure.
Foreign tranches of OCBC, DBS and UOB banks were off between 50 and 80 Singapore cents at S$18.10, S$18.40 and S$15.00 respectively.

Activity was brisk with 102.2 million shares traded. The morning's most active counter was new listing Poh Lian Holdings with 22 million shares traded, It stood at S$0.52 from its offer price of S$0.42. -- Nick Edwards (65 8703011)
